    transport: ""
    caSecretName: ""
    caSecretKey: ca.crt
    nodeCaFile: ""

# =============================================================================
# GATEWAY
# =============================================================================

gateway:
  # Internal URL used by colocated runtime processes such as Buster and the
  # gateway runtime. Empty defaults to http://127.0.0.1:<gateway.port>.
  url: ""
  # Run OpenClaw doctor --fix as a blocking init migration while the gateway is
  # stopped. New OpenClaw releases can require state-schema migrations before
  # the gateway is able to expose a healthy endpoint.
  startupDoctor:
    enabled: true
    # Keep V8 below the container memory limit while allowing OpenClaw's
    # configuration and SQLite migrations to process larger persistent state.
    nodeOptions: "--max-old-space-size=768"
    resources:
      requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 128Mi }
      limits: { cpu: 1000m, memory: 1Gi }
  command:
    - "node"
    - "/app/openclaw.mjs"
    - "gateway"
    - "--bind"
    - "lan"
    - "--port"
    - "18789"
  port: 18789
  bridgePort: 18790
  resources: {}

# Resource budget for setup work such as the offline OpenClaw plugin install.
# This init container runs before all application containers, so its resources
# are not concurrent with the gateway and runtime sidecars.
initSetup:
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 256Mi }
    limits: { cpu: 1000m, memory: 2Gi }

# Official external plugins are resolved by their pinned npm provenance while
# npm remains in offline mode against the cache baked into the gateway image.
# The install-mode marker forces a one-time repair when provenance rules change.
pluginSeed:
  installMode: "official-npm-v3-authoritative-reseed"
  specs:
    - "npm:@openclaw/acpx@2026.10.3"
    - "npm:@openclaw/discord@2026.10.3"

# =============================================================================
# CAPABILITY PROVIDERS
# =============================================================================

# Remote agent roles that provide capabilities to this deployment. Provider
# Services follow the chart's canonical `agent-<role>` naming contract.
capabilityProviders: {}
  # buster:
  #   agentRole: buster
  #   capabilities:
  #     runtime.dispatch:
  #       adapter: openclaw
  #       port: 18789
  #     test.plan.execute:
  #       adapter: buster-plan-v1
  #       port: 18891

# -- Replica count (always 1 per agent — agents are stateful)
replicaCount: 1

workerTrust:
  spiffe:
    enabled: false
    trustDomain: kubeclaw.internal
    socketPath: /run/spire/sockets/spire-agent.sock
    csiDriver: csi.spiffe.io
    envoy:
      repository: envoyproxy/envoy
      tag: v1.39.0
      digest: "sha256:d59f7f5fa10cff6d5892b6c5e7df5c9297ddfb2c3683e33fbfb82da24de4fa66"
      pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      resources:
        requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi }
        limits: { cpu: 500m, memory: 256Mi }

# =============================================================================
# AUTHENTICATION
# =============================================================================
# Gateway tokens authenticate API access to each agent.
# REQUIRED: Provide either token directly or via existingSecret.
# For production, always use existingSecret with SOPS or sealed-secrets.

auth:
  # Direct token (NOT recommended for production)
  token: ""
  # Reference an existing K8s secret
  existingSecret: ""
  existingSecretKey: "gatewayToken"

# =============================================================================
# MEMORY SEARCH EMBEDDING ENDPOINT (LiteLLM)
# =============================================================================
# LiteLLM is used only as the OpenAI-compatible remote embedding endpoint for
# OpenClaw memory search. Agent reasoning uses the managed OpenAI route directly.

litellm:
  endpoint: "http://litellm.kubeclaw.svc.cluster.local:4000/v1"
  # Direct API key (NOT recommended for production)
  apiKey: ""
  # Reference an existing K8s secret
  existingSecret: ""
  existingSecretKey: "litellmApiKey"

# =============================================================================
# STITCH API (Google Stitch MCP — UI design tool for Prism)
# =============================================================================

stitch:
  # Reference an existing K8s secret containing the Stitch API key
  existingSecret: ""
  existingSecretKey: "stitchApiKey"

# =============================================================================
# DISCORD INTEGRATION (optional)
# =============================================================================

discord:
  requireMention: true
  enabled: false
  channelId: ""
  # Discord user IDs allowed to approve exec commands (array of "user:<id>" strings)
  execApprovers: []
  # Direct token
  token: ""
  # Or reference existing secret
  existingSecret: ""
  existingSecretKey: "discordToken"

discordWebhook:
  secretName: ""
  secretKey: "discordWebhook"

# =============================================================================
# GIT CONFIGURATION
# =============================================================================

agent:
  # Active project name — sets CURRENT_PROJECT env for memory scoping
  project: ""  # e.g. "kubecommand"
  model:
    primary: "openai/gpt-5.6-sol"
    fallbacks:
      - "openai/gpt-5.5"
  git:
    # Enables chart-managed repository sync and SSH credentials. Disabling keeps
    # existing workspace data and removes Git init steps, mounts and Secret needs.
    enabled: true
    # Required only when enabled: K8s secret containing the SSH deploy key
    secretName: ""  # e.g. "git-deploy-key-nova"
    repoUrl: ""     # e.g. "git@github.com:your-org/your-project.git"

# =============================================================================
# INFRASTRUCTURE CONNECTIONS
# =============================================================================

# -- Redis (inter-agent messaging via Redis Streams)
# Infrastructure is deployed separately. Configure connection here.
redis:
  host: "redis-master.kubeclaw.svc.cluster.local"
  port: "6379"
  secretName: "redis-secrets"
  secretKey: "redis-password"

# =============================================================================
# =============================================================================
# WORKSPACE FILES
# =============================================================================
# Agent personality and operating procedures, mounted as markdown files.
# Define inline here or in your instance values file.
# See examples/workspace-templates/ for reference configurations.

workspace:
  enabled: true
  # false = only write files on first deploy (OpenClaw edits are preserved across restarts)
  # true  = overwrite from values on every restart (useful during initial development)
  overrideOnRestart: false
  soul: ""       # SOUL.md — personality, tone, core directives
  agents: ""     # AGENTS.md — protocols, workflow, delegation rules
  user: ""       # USER.md — information about the human operator
  tools: ""      # TOOLS.md — available tools and usage patterns
  memory: ""     # MEMORY.md — long-term context
  identity: ""   # IDENTITY.md — agent identity (filled at first run)
  bootstrap: ""  # BOOTSTRAP.md — first-run ritual (self-deleting)

# =============================================================================
# SERVICE
# =============================================================================

service:
  type: ClusterIP
  gatewayPort: 18789
  gatewayTargetPort: gateway
  bridgeEnabled: true
  bridgePort: 18790
  # NodePort for gateway when service.type is NodePort.
  nodePort: 0
  bridgeNodePort: 0
  # Extra ports to expose on the internal Service.
  # If nodePort is set while service.type is not NodePort, the chart also
  # creates a dedicated NodePort Service for that extra port without exposing
  # the gateway.
  extraPorts: []
  # Archviewer uses its own private Service; configure archviewer below.

# =============================================================================
# PERSISTENCE
# =============================================================================

persistence:
  config:
    enabled: true
    size: 10Gi
    storageClass: ""  # Uses cluster default if empty
    accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  workspace:
    enabled: true
    size: 20Gi
    storageClass: ""
    accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]

# =============================================================================
# RESOURCES
# =============================================================================

resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 200m
    memory: 512Mi
  limits:
    cpu: 2000m
    memory: 2Gi

# =============================================================================
# SECURITY
# =============================================================================
# OpenClaw's base image requires root. Set to false only if running a custom
# rootless image. Containers remain non-privileged in either mode.

runAsRoot: true

# =============================================================================
# HEALTH CHECKS
# =============================================================================

probes:
  startup:
    enabled: true
    initialDelaySeconds: 10
    periodSeconds: 10
    timeoutSeconds: 10
    failureThreshold: 24
  readiness:
    enabled: true
    initialDelaySeconds: 5
    periodSeconds: 10
    timeoutSeconds: 10
    failureThreshold: 3
  liveness:
    enabled: true
    initialDelaySeconds: 120
    periodSeconds: 15
    timeoutSeconds: 5
    failureThreshold: 3
  dependencies:
    gateway:
      enabled: true
    redis:
      enabled: true
    redisStream:
      enabled: true
      stream: ""
      maxLen: 1000
    litellm:
      enabled: true
    registries:
      enabled: true
      endpoints:
        - "http://registry-local.kubeclaw.svc.cluster.local:5001"
        - "http://registry-mirror.kubeclaw.svc.cluster.local:5000"
# =============================================================================
# SHUTDOWN
# =============================================================================

shutdown:

  # Redis task settlement, active-session termination, and lease cleanup.
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 180
  drainFile: "/tmp/kubeclaw-draining"
  preStopDrainSeconds: 5

# =============================================================================
# SERVICE ACCOUNT
# =============================================================================
# When enabled, creates an agent ServiceAccount. By default it does not mount a
# Kubernetes token. Buster deployments that need Kubernetes suite access use
# busterNamespaceBroker; the chart projects a lease-client token only into the
# pipeline sidecar and keeps the gateway token-free.

serviceAccount:
  create: false
  automount: false

# =============================================================================
# BUSTER NAMESPACE BROKER (Buster only)
# =============================================================================
# Self-contained namespace lease controller for Buster k8s tests.
# Buster can create BusterNamespaceLease objects in the release namespace; the
# trusted controller creates/deletes ephemeral test namespaces and binds Buster's
# ServiceAccount only inside those namespaces.

busterNamespaceBroker:
  enabled: false
  # Grants the agent ServiceAccount permission to request ephemeral test
  # namespaces through BusterNamespaceLease CRs. Buster gets this permission
  # whenever broker mode is enabled. Other roles, such as Nova E2E, must opt in
  # explicitly and still do not receive namespace/workload authority.
  leaseClient:
    enabled: false
    verificationRead:
      enabled: false
      # Existing operator namespace; shared by the scoped RBAC and agent probe.
      # The agent release does not create or own this namespace or Secret.
      tailscaleOperatorNamespace: tailscale
      tailscaleOAuthSecretName: operator-oauth
  # Opt-in trusted Nova runtime only; same-container code is not isolated by this mount.
  readyClient:
    enabled: false
    endpoint: ""
    audience: ""
    caSecretName: ""
  leaseApiGroup: kubeclaw.forgestack.ai
  leaseApiVersion: v1alpha1
  allowedPrefixes:
    - test
  defaultTtlSeconds: 7200
  maxTtlSeconds: 86400
  controller:
    # Independent human-decision authority; empty configuration denies all.
    productDecisions:
      enabled: false
      audience: ""
      producerNamespace: ""
      producerServiceAccount: ""
      issuer: ""
      verifyKey: "" # Raw Ed25519 public key, standard base64; never a signing key.
      allowedActors: []
    readiness:
      enabled: false
      audience: ""
      producerNamespace: ""
      producerServiceAccount: ""
      tlsSecretName: ""
    # A lease can bind only these service accounts and access modes. Each lease
    # must explicitly request its subjects; no agent is added to all namespaces.
    allowedAccess:
      # Subjects without a namespace are resolved in the Helm release namespace.
      - subject: agent-buster
        modes: [deployer, tester]
      - subject: agent-nova
        modes: [deployer]
    # Only these Secrets can be copied from the release namespace into a test
    # namespace. Test-login Secrets are created separately and scoped by name.
    allowedSourceSecrets: []
    image:
      repository: ghcr.io/datrab/kubeclaw-namespace-controller
      tag: latest
      pullPolicy: Always
    pollIntervalMs: 3000
    resources:
      requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 128Mi }
      limits: { cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi }

# =============================================================================
# COMMANDS
# =============================================================================

commands:
  # Channel-qualified operator IDs for OpenClaw owner-only commands.
  # Example: ["discord:123456789012345678"]
  ownerAllowFrom: []
  # Discord user IDs allowed to use DMs, commands, and guild channels. Bare,
  # "user:", and "discord:" forms are accepted here; guild policy renders
  # canonical bare IDs under channels.discord.guilds.*.users.
  allowFromDiscord: []

# =============================================================================
# Platform-level config for the pipeline engine.

  overrideOnRestart: false

swarmConfigJson: ""

semgrepConfigYaml: ""

#           'no-alert': 'warn',
#         },
#       },

eslintConfigMjs: ""

# =============================================================================
# CUSTOM SKILLS (optional)
# =============================================================================
# KubeClaw system skills (redis.ts, memory.js, pipeline.ts, etc.) are delivered
# by code bundles. This section is ONLY for additional user-defined skills.

# Example:

customSkills: {}

# =============================================================================
# SCHEDULING
# =============================================================================

nodeSelector: {}
tolerations: []
podAnnotations: {}
extraEnv: []

# -- Extra sidecar containers to inject into the agent pod (e.g. archviewer)

  hostname: nova-architecture

extraVolumes: []

busterRuntimePersistence:

images:

  resources: { requests: { cpu: 250m, memory: 256Mi }, limits: { cpu: "2", memory: 2Gi } }

name: Build Ops Images
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - versions.json
      - scripts/versions.mjs
      - scripts/scan-runtime-images.sh
      - tools/ops-mcp/**
      - my-values/infra/**
      - scripts/*cilium*
      - examples/cilium/**
      - ops/pod/**
      - charts/ops-pod/**
      - scripts/deploy-ops-pod.sh
      - .github/workflows/build-ops-mcp.yaml
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - versions.json
      - scripts/versions.mjs
      - scripts/scan-runtime-images.sh
      - tools/ops-mcp/**
      - my-values/infra/**
      - scripts/*cilium*
      - examples/cilium/**
      - ops/pod/**
      - charts/ops-pod/**
      - scripts/deploy-ops-pod.sh
      - .github/workflows/build-ops-mcp.yaml
  workflow_dispatch: null
concurrency:
  group: ops-mcp-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - image: kubeclaw-ops-mcp
            context: tools/ops-mcp
          - image: kubeclaw-codex-ops
            context: ops/pod
    env:
      IMAGE_NAME: ${{ matrix.image }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          package-manager-cache: false
      - name: Check central runtime versions
        run: node scripts/versions.mjs --check
      - name: Test Ops MCP

set -euo pipefail

readonly TRIVY_VERSION="0.74.0"
readonly TRIVY_AMD64_SHA256="2ae6fe3ee734b7fdf11335663e18c75ea12dccc76062f09f164a3b0f8be4371a"
readonly TRIVY_ARM64_SHA256="b94ce1976bbf3c15b514b605ee88be7c6d94a29be2302847ff01cb794d47aad5"

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: scripts/scan-runtime-images.sh IMAGE@sha256:DIGEST [IMAGE@sha256:DIGEST ...]

Scan published runtime images with the pinned Trivy release.
Use --executable to install/verify Trivy and print its executable path.

Private GHCR images require TRIVY_USERNAME and TRIVY_PASSWORD, or valid
registry credentials in the local container configuration.

Optional environment variables:
  KUBECLAW_TRIVY_REPORT_DIR  Report directory. Default: dist/trivy
  KUBECLAW_TOOL_CACHE        Tool cache. Default: XDG cache or a temporary cache.
  XDG_CACHE_HOME             Optional cache parent directory.
EOF
}

require_command() {
  if ! command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Required command is unavailable: $1" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

install_trivy() {
  local machine="$1"
  local archive_arch archive_sha
  case "$machine" in
    x86_64|amd64)
      archive_arch="64bit"
      archive_sha="$TRIVY_AMD64_SHA256"
      ;;
    aarch64|arm64)
      archive_arch="ARM64"
      archive_sha="$TRIVY_ARM64_SHA256"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Unsupported architecture: $machine" >&2
      exit 1
